Jasons élections dans les bureaux de La: Let’s Talk Elections at La Converse’s Offices - Dialogues
Que pensent nos communautés des élection: What do our communities think about the elections? We discussed it at our election night event
La soirée, animée par le journaliste Cyr: The evening, hosted by journalist Cyrille Ekwalla and La Converse journalists, began with a political quiz for the young people in the room. It was a fun way to break the ice and get participants ready for an open dialogue on Canadian politics and the particularities of the election campaign.
Les journalistes de La Converse ont ensu: La Converse journalists then shared their experiences and observations from covering the election campaign. Their accounts opened the door to lively discussions on a range of themes, from political representation to civic engagement. Many participants questioned the effectiveness of the current electoral system, the lack of representation of racialized communities, and the absence of issues affecting marginalized communities.
“I don’t believe in the political system. I don’t even think it represents the majority of the population well. Every election, I don’t feel represented. (...) The electoral system isn’t made for people who look like me or who come from neighbourhoods like Côte-des-Neiges, Saint-Michel or Montréal-Nord. (...)” one participant said. It was a feeling shared by several people present that night. His remarks sparked an exchange on the need to reform the system so that it can better serve marginalized voices.
Un autre participant a abordé la questio: Another participant raised the question of voting culture within immigrant communities: “The problem with people from immigrant backgrounds is that most of the parents who come here fled a corrupt system, so they don’t pass on a culture of voting to their kids. Even though young people in these communities like politics and talk about it, when it comes time to go vote, they don’t have that culture of voting.”
La soirée a également permis d’aborder l: The evening also touched on the Latin American vote in Montréal, the coverage of First Nations issues during the campaign, and Haitian asylum seekers – an issue co-opted by a whole segment of the political class, according to one participant.
« On entend beaucoup de gens qui disent: “You hear a lot of people saying they’re going to vote strategically,” added a young participant who was voting for the first time. She spoke about how complicated it is to make an electoral choice in a political landscape that sometimes feels foreign to her.
À la suite des discussions, la soirée de: After the discussions, election night coverage was screened live, allowing participants to follow the results in a relaxed atmosphere.
Cette soirée a donné à entendre des voix: The evening brought out voices that at times clashed – notably on whether or not voting is necessary, or on what message to give younger people about it – but that all agreed on one point: the insufficient representation of racialized communities in these elections.
